content.comment_body: Using [product_name] V8.0.0 and a [article_no] Standard module, I am able to send the program to the PLC and the online test functions correctly. However, if I read the same program from the PLC back into [product_name] (without any modifications), attempting an online test results in a message that the PC and PLC programs differ. Since my customer intends to monitor the program, uploading it is not a practical solution. Is there a way to address this issue?
Have you tried uploading a simple program, such as connecting an input to activate an output, to check whether the problem stems from the programming or possibly the hardware itself?

The issue you've described can sometimes occur after downloading the program to the [product_name] and then modifying display parameter values, like changing a delay value or a numerical parameter in an arithmetic instruction. This results in the error during an online test, even though the actual logic remains unchanged—only the parameters differ. To run the online test in such cases, the program should be loaded from the original license, and a new chart started before beginning the test. Changing parameters during an online test works, but the problem you mention doesn't match this scenario as far as I know.
When I send the program to the PLC, monitoring works perfectly. But after reading the exact same program back from the PLC, without any changes, monitoring fails.

Have you verified that the selected [version_no] module in [product_name] matches the hardware you're connected to? There are several releases of the [version_no]. In [product_name] V8, you can check the hardware selection by clicking on the [company_name] symbol in the lower corner. Try each available module, or check the hardware unit for its release marker. Regarding your customer: Ensure they have at least [product_name] V8, since older versions might not support the latest hardware release (ES4 is the newest). If they can't select ES4, they should update [product_name] V8. An upgrade is recommended.
To solve the issue, select the correct hardware option: go to tools, then hardware, and choose [article_no]-ES4. This should resolve your problem.

I've previously tried that approach and encountered a different error indicating incompatibility. Now, connecting as 'standard' gives me the incompatibility error and connecting as 'ES4' triggers the program mismatch error. Could you clarify what ES4 refers to? Ultimately, I found a working alternative called [product_name] Monitor Multi, which works well. While it offers fewer features, the other version can still monitor older modules. No need for [product_name] software in this case. Downloaded from: [url] Thanks for all the suggestions.
If the error were due to an incorrect firmware version, a different message would likely appear. See: [url] ESx refers to the release number of the product.

The term [version_no] ES4 stands for [version_no] with release E-Stand 4 or higher. It's important to match this setting to your connected hardware, otherwise the online test will fail with incompatibility errors. Also, if comparing the program on your PC with what's on the module in [product_name], you may see differences if someone has changed modifiable values such as message text or parameters via the module’s interface. Hope this clarifies things.

I've tried that procedure and encountered incompatible hardware errors. Now, the 'standard' selection results in incompatibility and 'ES4' selection causes a program mismatch. What does ES4 mean? In any case, I found a working copy of [product_name] Monitor Multi, which functions well. Though it is limited in features, another version supports monitoring older modules. No need for [product_name] in this scenario. Download available at: [url] Note: This is a trial version limited to ten minutes per session. For full functionality, it's best to use [product_name] for general monitoring purposes.

How did you discover this? I didn’t find any indication of a 10-minute limitation, and the official [company_name] website doesn’t mention this. According to [company_name], the limitation is that transferring programs or performing online tests is not possible. Reference: [url]

I'm not referring to [company_name] [product_name] V8 or newer. I'm talking about the software mentioned above, [product_name] Monitor trial version, which restricts monitoring to 10 minutes per session. For best results, use [product_name] V8 for monitoring, downloading, uploading, and online testing.

Yes, the download is a trial version allowing you to monitor for only 10 minutes at a time, and costs about $50, offered out of the Netherlands. Back to compatibility: I can send and monitor using [product_name] without issue, but reading the exact same program back only seconds later shows differences, even when nothing was changed. I haven’t tried direct PC-to-PLC connection (currently working via office network), but since it's unlikely a speed issue, I didn't pursue it.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion centers on issues with program mismatch errors during online testing in [product_name] V8 when working with hardware modules, particularly regarding correct hardware revision (release) matching. Users are confused by differing error messages and unclear distinctions between parameter changes and logic changes. As a workaround, some resort to third-party monitoring software with limited features when the official tool doesn't meet expectations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable and consistent monitoring features in [product_name], with seamless version matching between software and hardware modules. There’s also a desire for simple workflows without extra uploads for end customers, and clear, informative error messages whenever mismatches or incompatibilities occur.
